title: Diabetes – Key Facts and Prevention
raw_summary:
Diabetes is a sickness where the body can't use sugar rightly in our blood, which comes from food we eat and drinks like soda or juice with lots of sugar. This happens because either not enough insulin (a special help hormone) is made by pancreas or used properly to control this sugar level. Too much sugar can hurt many parts inside us over time, especially nerves that feel touch and pain in our feet leading sometimes even to losing a foot if it gets infected badly from sores not healing well because of diabetes damage.

In 2014, about one out of every twenty adults had this sickness called Diabetes worldwide. It causes many deaths each year and is the reason for kidney problems too. People with it have a higher chance to get heart attacks or strokes because their blood vessels are damaged by sugar over time.

title: About Influenza (Flu) – Symptoms, Spread, and Prevention
raw_summary:
The flu is an illness from viruses that affects our nose, throat, and sometimes lungs. It can make people feel sick or even cause death in some cases. The good news? Getting a yearly shot helps prevent it. Every season in the U.S., millions get this virus causing 140 to 710 thousand hospital visits and up to half a million fatalities annually since 2010, showing its heavy impact on healthcare each year.

Flu spreads when sick people cough or sneeze near others who then breathe in the virus-filled droplets. It's also possible for someone else to get it by touching a contaminated surface and then their mouth, nose, or eyes. Most healthy adults can pass on flu about 1 day before symptoms appear until up to 7 days after getting sick themselves. Children under two years old are especially infectious longer than this period.

title: High Blood Pressure (Hypertension) – Causes, Risks and Treatment
raw_summary:
High blood pressure is a sneaky problem that doesn't always show symptoms but can cause big problems like heart attacks if ignored. About one in three adults in the UK has it, and many don't know because they feel fine. Adults over forty should check their blood pressure every five years to catch any issues early on.

Blood pressure is measured with two numbers that tell how hard your heart works and if there’s resistance against blood flowing through vessels. Normal range is between 90/60mmHg and 120/80mmHg, while high readings could mean trouble ahead without changes to keep it under control.

Several things can raise your risk of having too much pressure in the arteries: getting older than sixty-five years old, being overweight or not exercising enough are some factors that play a role along with diet and lifestyle habits like drinking alcohol excessively. Eating less salt and more fruits and veggies can help lower risks of high blood pressure developing further down the road.

title: Malaria – Key Facts, Prevention, and Treatment
raw_summary:
Malaria hurts people, mostly those living where mosquitoes live a lot. It's caused by tiny germs from bugs called Plasmodium parasites that bite humans when they sleep at night or early in the morning. Malaria can make you feel sick with fever and chills but sometimes it is very bad, making people confused, tired, having seizures, or trouble breathing. Babies, young kids, pregnant women who are not immune to malaria, those living with HIV/AIDS, travelers from places without mosquitoes and some countries in Africa have a higher risk of getting very sick from it. In 2022 alone, about half the world's cases happened on this continent; sadly, many children under five died because they got malaria there too.

Mosquito nets treated with insect spray and indoor spaces where mosquitoes can’t live are ways to stop these bugs from spreading disease in communities around the world.

title: Mental Health – Understanding and Coping with Stress
raw_summary:
Stress happens when life's problems get too much to handle. It can make you feel anxious or sad if it goes on long enough, which is not good for the body either. Stress makes our heart race and blood pressure go up as a way of protecting us from danger. But in today’s world with lots going wrong all at once, this alarm system doesn't always turn off properly.

When stress stays too much on your mind or body over time, it can lead to high blood pressure, heart problems and changes that might cause anxiety or depression. It could even make people gain weight because of the hormones in our bodies called cortisol. Stress is a big problem for many adults' health as they feel its effects on their body and mind very strongly.

You can tell stress by feeling headaches, muscle pain, or changes like eating too much or not enough. It might make you anxious, sad, angry, irritable, tired easily, have trouble sleeping well, avoid friends and family, exercise less often, or change how food makes you feel in your stomach.
